halloween.house_exterior.abundant.source.instructionText: Edit only the target house, the building in the center of the image, and its own yard in the attached photo to show a lavish, over-the-top American Halloween display covering the target home and its yard: the house the whole neighborhood comes to see, in the lighting of the original photograph. Keep the same camera position, crop, perspective and lens, the roof outline, doors, windows, siding color and texture, trim, steps, railings, landscaping, sky, time of day, parked vehicles and every neighboring building exactly as photographed. Only decorations are added, and there are a great many of them. Decorate only what this photo shows of the house: each sentence below applies only where the photo already shows the thing it names, and is skipped where it does not. Outline every roof edge, eave and gable of the target house and every window with orange and purple string lights, closely spaced. Stretch thick white cobwebs with large black spiders across the corners of the windows and the walls, and across a porch, railings, columns and shrubs that are already there, and set one giant black spider on the wall or roof. If a front door is visible, outline its frame with the lights and hang a black wreath with an orange bow on it, leaving the door itself as it is, with flocks of black bat silhouettes on the walls around it. Beside steps, a porch and a path that are already there, crowd carved jack-o'-lanterns of many sizes, all glowing from inside, with piles of pumpkins and gourds, hay bales, corn stalks tied to columns that are already there and pots of orange and purple mums, without hiding or replacing what stands there. On open lawn or bare ground of its own yard, stand several posed plastic skeletons and a few white sheet ghosts on stakes among more glowing pumpkins, and hang small ghosts and lanterns from the branches of trees that are already there. Add no door, steps, railing, porch, path, wall, window, shrub, hedge or tree of your own: only decorations. Every light on the decorations is switched on and visibly glowing. Use believable real-world scale, secure attachments and contact shadows that match the existing light, so that it looks like a real photograph of real, professionally installed decorations. Keep the lighting, sky and time of day of the original photograph. Leave any blurred or pixelated areas, people, vehicles and license plates exactly as they appear; do not sharpen, reconstruct or replace them. No gore, blood, weapons, corpses or tombstones, no cartoon or licensed characters, no inflatables, no sugar skulls, no text, no people, no fog or sky effects, no snow unless present, no new structures, nothing on neighboring homes, on the sidewalk or on the street. Also add no pets, brand logos or religious symbols. Do not alter or cover house numbers, signs or logos. A listed decoration may replace an existing wreath, planter or hanging basket at its spot. Keep the doors, the steps and the paths clear to walk on. Return the same photograph with these decorations added.
